# B8 Release Candidate 1 (B8-rc1)

After many months of hard work from our team, I am pleased to announce Beta 8 Release Candidate 1.

B8 is a major update that introduces the Looking Glass Indirect Display Driver, direct input and clipboard transport, a new USB audio path, end-to-end HDR support, and extensive latency and reliability improvements.

As this is a release candidate, please report any regressions or other issues encountered during testing.

If you like this project, find it useful, and would like to help support its continued development, you can do so using the following platforms:

- [GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/gnif)
- [Ko-Fi](https://ko-fi.com/lookingglass)
- [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/gnif)
- [PayPal](https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr?cmd=_s-xclick&hosted_button_id=ESQ72XUPGKXRY)
- BTC — `14ZFcYjsKPiVreHqcaekvHGL846u3ZuT13`
- ETH — `0x6f8aEe454384122bF9ed28f025FBCe2Bce98db85`
- XMR — `47xM4zG7b2tEj4mnSywHve4ydZzn3wzhf22snDRB7aSEcXrgUBpoT2Z4phTnyFMi1sMyQtHbdufMYRQ2PzMn3PGUJAE1dpc`

## Important Upgrade Information

B8 introduces protocol changes that are not compatible with B7. The Looking Glass client, IDD, and OBS plugin must use matching versions.

The legacy Host Application remains available as a B7 workflow. Users who require it should retain the complete B7 client, Host Application, and OBS stack rather than mixing B7 and B8 components.

B8 requires Windows 10 version 1903 or newer. HDR and wide-color support normally require compatible Windows 11 IddCx interfaces. Windows 10 continues to use the SDR-compatible path.

## Major New Features

### Looking Glass IDD

The Looking Glass Indirect Display Driver is now the recommended Windows server. It creates its own virtual monitor, eliminating the need for a physical display or dummy plug.

The IDD uses Direct3D 12 for accelerated capture and processing when a suitable GPU is available. An SDR software fallback supports systems without a usable render GPU.

A new installer includes the display driver, direct-input driver, tray helper, and optional IVSHMEM driver installation. It can also disable the legacy Host Application during migration.

The configuration interface supports custom resolutions, fractional refresh rates up to 1000 Hz, preferred and default modes, dynamic guest resolution, configuration reload and rollback, processing status, and workarounds for problematic GPU drivers.

### Direct Input and Clipboard

Keyboard and mouse input can now travel directly over LGMP using the Looking Glass virtual HID device. This supports absolute desktop input, relative captured input, media keys, up to 32 mouse buttons, and keyboard lock-state synchronization.

Clipboard synchronization also runs directly over LGMP and supports bidirectional text, images, and file transfers on both X11 and Wayland. Transfers are streamed and pipelined to keep clipboard control responsive while large files are being copied.

SPICE remains available as a fallback, but is no longer required for primary IDD input or clipboard operation.

### USB Audio

Looking Glass can now present an emulated USB Audio Class 2 device to Windows through a SPICE USB-redirection channel.

It supports stereo, quadraphonic, 5.1, and 7.1 playback using 24-bit PCM at up to 192 kHz, along with microphone recording and asynchronous clock feedback. Classic SPICE audio remains available as a compatibility fallback.

Audio buffering, synchronization, underrun recovery, and microphone privacy handling have also been substantially improved.

### HDR and Color Management

B8 adds end-to-end HDR and wide-color support. The IDD transports HDR metadata and the Windows display color transform, while the EGL renderer can either present native HDR or tone-map it for an SDR display.
